From a4376d9a5d4c9610e69def3fc0b32c86a7ab7a41 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Shin'ichiro Kawasaki <shinichiro.kawasaki@wdc.com>
Date: Sun, 1 Mar 2026 21:17:04 +0900
Subject: [PATCH] btrfs: fix leak of kobject name for sub-group space_info

When create_space_info_sub_group() allocates elements of
space_info->sub_group[], kobject_init_and_add() is called for each
element via btrfs_sysfs_add_space_info_type(). However, when
check_removing_space_info() frees these elements, it does not call
btrfs_sysfs_remove_space_info() on them. As a result, kobject_put() is
not called and the associated kobj->name objects are leaked.

This memory leak is reproduced by running the blktests test case
zbd/009 on kernels built with CONFIG_DEBUG_KMEMLEAK. The kmemleak
feature reports the following error:

unreferenced object 0xffff888112877d40 (size 16):
  comm "mount", pid 1244, jiffies 4294996972
  hex dump (first 16 bytes):
    64 61 74 61 2d 72 65 6c 6f 63 00 c4 c6 a7 cb 7f  data-reloc......
  backtrace (crc 53ffde4d):
    __kmalloc_node_track_caller_noprof+0x619/0x870
    kstrdup+0x42/0xc0
    kobject_set_name_vargs+0x44/0x110
    kobject_init_and_add+0xcf/0x150
    btrfs_sysfs_add_space_info_type+0xfc/0x210 [btrfs]
    create_space_info_sub_group.constprop.0+0xfb/0x1b0 [btrfs]
    create_space_info+0x211/0x320 [btrfs]
    btrfs_init_space_info+0x15a/0x1b0 [btrfs]
    open_ctree+0x33c7/0x4a50 [btrfs]
    btrfs_get_tree.cold+0x9f/0x1ee [btrfs]
    vfs_get_tree+0x87/0x2f0
    vfs_cmd_create+0xbd/0x280
    __do_sys_fsconfig+0x3df/0x990
    do_syscall_64+0x136/0x1540
    entry_SYSCALL_64_after_hwframe+0x76/0x7e

To avoid the leak, call btrfs_sysfs_remove_space_info() instead of
kfree() for the elements.

Fixes: f92ee31e031c ("btrfs: introduce btrfs_space_info sub-group")
Link: https://lore.kernel.org/linux-block/b9488881-f18d-4f47-91a5-3c9bf63955a5@wdc.com/
Reviewed-by: Johannes Thumshirn <johannes.thumshirn@wdc.com>
Signed-off-by: Shin'ichiro Kawasaki <shinichiro.kawasaki@wdc.com>
Signed-off-by: David Sterba <dsterba@suse.com>

diff --git a/fs/btrfs/block-group.c b/fs/btrfs/block-group.c
index fa55d868ecd8..f7fcff7dca8f 100644
--- a/fs/btrfs/block-group.c
+++ b/fs/btrfs/block-group.c
@@ -4584,7 +4584,7 @@ static void check_removing_space_info(struct btrfs_space_info *space_info)
 		for (int i = 0; i < BTRFS_SPACE_INFO_SUB_GROUP_MAX; i++) {
 			if (space_info->sub_group[i]) {
 				check_removing_space_info(space_info->sub_group[i]);
-				kfree(space_info->sub_group[i]);
+				btrfs_sysfs_remove_space_info(space_info->sub_group[i]);
 				space_info->sub_group[i] = NULL;
 			}
 		}
-- 
2.34.1

## Summary of Modifications

### File Modified: `fs/btrfs/block-group.c`

**Change:** In the function `check_removing_space_info()`, the code that frees sub-group space_info elements was updated.

- **Before:**  
  `kfree(space_info->sub_group[i]);`  
  This directly freed the memory for the sub-group structure but did not release the associated kobject name allocated via `kobject_init_and_add()`.

- **After:**  
  `btrfs_sysfs_remove_space_info(space_info->sub_group[i]);`  
  This function properly tears down the kobject (via `kobject_put()`), which frees the kobject name and prevents a memory leak.

### Relationships Between Modifications

The single modification directly addresses the memory leak described in the commit. The leak occurred because `kobject_init_and_add()` (called during sub-group creation via `btrfs_sysfs_add_space_info_type()`) stores a dynamically allocated name (`kobj->name`) in the kobject. When the sub-group was freed using only `kfree()`, the kobject's release mechanism was not triggered, leaving the name allocated. By replacing `kfree()` with `btrfs_sysfs_remove_space_info()` (which internally calls `kobject_del()` and `kobject_put()`), the kobject is properly released, ensuring the name is freed. This change is self-contained and fixes the leak for all sub-group elements within the `check_removing_space_info()` cleanup loop.

btrfs: fix leak of kobject name for sub-group space_info

When create_space_info_sub_group() allocates elements of

  hex dump (first 16 bytes):

    kstrdup+0x42/0xc0
    kobject_set_name_vargs+0x44/0x110
    kobject_init_and_add+0xcf/0x150
    btrfs_sysfs_add_space_info_type+0xfc/0x210 [btrfs]
    create_space_info_sub_group.constprop.0+0xfb/0x1b0 [btrfs]
    create_space_info+0x211/0x320 [btrfs]
    btrfs_init_space_info+0x15a/0x1b0 [btrfs]

    vfs_get_tree+0x87/0x2f0
    vfs_cmd_create+0xbd/0x280

    do_syscall_64+0x136/0x1540
    entry_SYSCALL_64_after_hwframe+0x76/0x7e

To avoid the leak, call btrfs_sysfs_remove_space_info() instead of
kfree() for the elements.

Fixes: f92ee31e031c ("btrfs: introduce btrfs_space_info sub-group")
Link: https://lore.kernel.org/linux-block/b9488881-f18d-4f47-91a5-3c9bf63955a5@wdc.com/
Reviewed-by: Johannes Thumshirn <johannes.thumshirn@wdc.com>
Signed-off-by: Shin'ichiro Kawasaki <shinichiro.kawasaki@wdc.com>
Signed-off-by: David Sterba <dsterba@suse.com>

Here is the root cause:
The function check_removing_space_info() in fs/btrfs/block-group.c used kfree() to free sub_group space_info structures, but did not call btrfs_sysfs_remove_space_info() to properly release the kobject and its associated name, causing a memory leak.

Here is the patch:
 
 static void check_removing_space_info(struct btrfs_space_info *space_info)
 {
 	struct btrfs_fs_info *info = space_info->fs_info;
 
 	if (space_info->subgroup_id == BTRFS_SUB_GROUP_PRIMARY) {
 		/* This is a top space_info, proceed with its children first. */
 		for (int i = 0; i < BTRFS_SPACE_INFO_SUB_GROUP_MAX; i++) {
 			if (space_info->sub_group[i]) {
 				check_removing_space_info(space_info->sub_group[i]);
-				kfree(space_info->sub_group[i]);
+				btrfs_sysfs_remove_space_info(space_info->sub_group[i]);
 				space_info->sub_group[i] = NULL;
 			}
 		}
 	}
 
 	/*
 	 * Do not hide this behind enospc_debug, this is actually important and
 	 * indicates a real bug if this happens.
 	 */
 	if (WARN_ON(space_info->bytes_pinned > 0 || space_info->bytes_may_use > 0))
 		btrfs_dump_space_info(space_info, 0, false);
 
 	/*
 	 * If there was a failure to cleanup a log tree, very likely due to an
 	 * IO failure on a writeback attempt of one or more of its extent
 	 * buffers, we could not do proper (and cheap) unaccounting of their
 	 * reserved space, so don't warn on bytes_reserved > 0 in that case.
 	 */
 	if (!(space_info->flags & BTRFS_BLOCK_GROUP_METADATA) ||
 	    !BTRFS_FS_LOG_CLEANUP_ERROR(info)) {
 		if (WARN_ON(space_info->bytes_reserved > 0))
 			btrfs_dump_space_info(space_info, 0, false);
 	}
 
 	WARN_ON(space_info->reclaim_size > 0);
 }

The code statements that lead to the bug are:
```

```
Reason:
The function `check_removing_space_info` frees the sub-group space_info structures using `kfree()`, but these structures were initialized with `kobject_init_and_add` (via `btrfs_sysfs_add_space_info_type`), which allocates a name string for the kobject. Using `kfree()` directly does not call `kobject_put()`, so the kobject's name memory is never freed, causing a leak.

The code statements that fix the bug are:
```
btrfs_sysfs_remove_space_info(space_info->sub_group[i]);
```
Reason:
`btrfs_sysfs_remove_space_info()` properly calls `kobject_put()` to release the kobject and its associated name string, preventing the memory leak. This ensures cleanup matches the initialization done by `btrfs_sysfs_add_space_info_type()`.
